decisions.site: Copper Creek Boat Access, NPS Road 213
decisions.coordinateRole: NPS public Copper Creek access/ramp-area point; not a surveyed gravel-ramp edge
decisions.reason: NPS identifies Copper Creek as the public take-out for the Skagit float and names Copper Creek among the launch areas. The saved point identifies the access site, while the manager sources do not publish a surveyed ramp-edge GPS. Retain it and clarify that the coordinate represents the ramp/access area; preserve the existing limited-parking and road-clearance instructions.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep all three route records; label the saved coordinate as an NPS access-area anchor and direct paddlers to the public gravel ramp.

decisions.site: Noblewood Park Boquet mouth cartop launch
decisions.resolvedSiteName: Noblewood Park cartop launch / Boquet mouth access area
decisions.coordinateRole: Empire State Water Trail site coordinate for the Noblewood Park cartop launch; not a surveyed wet-edge point
decisions.reason: The Empire State Water Trail identifies Noblewood Park as the cartop launch at the Boquet River mouth and publishes a site coordinate matching the saved point to its listed precision. No separate wet-edge survey was found. Keep the point as the launch-area anchor and retain seasonal-hours, fee, and beach-rule checks.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the current coordinate; name it as the park cartop-launch/access area and do not claim exact waterline precision.

decisions.coordinateRole: NYSDEC Sevey hand-launch access-area anchor; not a surveyed water-edge point
decisions.reason: Current NYSDEC Raquette Boreal Complex material identifies the Sevey hand launch and the seasonal-road context; the DEC complex map corroborates its location. The sources establish the public launch area but not a separate surveyed wet-edge coordinate. Keep the point and state its access-area role, seasonal approach, and carry check.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the coordinate as the DEC launch-area anchor; verify seasonal road, carry, waterline, and current signs before travel.

decisions.site: Turtle Creek Greenway Trail / Milwaukee Road
decisions.resolvedSiteName: Turtle Creek Greenway parking / river access above Milwaukee Road
decisions.coordinateRole: Greenway river-exit and parking access-area anchor; not a surveyed water-entry coordinate
decisions.reason: The City of Beloit identifies creek access and parking at the south end of the greenway, and its open-space material supports public greenway access. Wisconsin River Trips describes the shallow/gravel exit, steep bank, hidden trail, and roughly 350-foot grass carry to parking. The point is appropriately treated as a carry/parking access anchor, not moved toward a water line.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the coordinate, explicitly call it an access-area anchor, and retain the hidden-trail, steep-bank, and grass-carry instructions.

decisions.site: Historic Bridge Park public kayak launch
decisions.resolvedSiteName: Historic Bridge Park public kayak-launch access area
decisions.coordinateRole: Calhoun County public park/launch-area anchor; not a surveyed launch-edge coordinate
decisions.reason: Calhoun County's 2025–2029 Parks Master Plan and park brochure document a public kayak/canoe launch and parking at Historic Bridge Park. The county evidence verifies the facility, but does not establish the saved point as the precise launch edge. Retain the public access-area coordinate and describe it accordingly.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the park access-area point and clarify its role in route notes and provenance.

decisions.site: Hammocks Beach State Park designated paddle access
decisions.resolvedSiteName: Hammocks Beach State Park mainland kayak-launch area
decisions.coordinateRole: NC State Parks mainland park-access GPS; official park map identifies the designated kayak launch, but the GPS is not a surveyed water edge
decisions.reason: The current NC State Parks page and official park map establish the mainland paddle access and marked Huggins Island route. State Parks' fee schedule distinguishes the free kayak launch from boat-ramp fees. The selected point is a park-access GPS rather than a surveyed launch edge, so keep it, direct users to the marked self-launch, and distinguish kayak-launch fees from ramp fees.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the park GPS as an access-area anchor; use the marked mainland kayak launch and preserve tide, wind, ferry, and closure checks.

decisions.site: Dry Canyon boater take-out (BLM public water-entry edge)
decisions.resolvedSiteName: Dry Canyon boater take-out access area (BLM)
decisions.coordinateRole: BLM published Dry Canyon take-out and picnic-area GPS; not a surveyed river-edge coordinate
decisions.reason: BLM publishes 32.8922,-109.4921 for Dry Canyon Boat Take-Out and Picnic Area, calls it a public exit for Gila River floats, and describes the site facilities. The location is an access-site GPS, not the precise river edge, so remove the inaccurate 'water-entry edge' claim. BLM announced phased repairs beginning July 2026 with periodic partial restrictions expected for about six months, including at Dry Canyon; the current notice must be checked before travel.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the BLM take-out-area coordinate; clarify river-right landing/carry and parking checks, and surface the temporary repair restriction.

decisions.site: Riverside Kayak Park public dock and carry-in access
decisions.resolvedSiteName: Riverside Kayak Park / universal-access dock area
decisions.coordinateRole: Michigan Water Trails published Riverside park GPS; public universal-access dock is documented separately, and GPS is not a surveyed dock edge
decisions.reason: Michigan Water Trails documents the public Paw Paw River access, universal-access dock, parking, and carry under 50 yards, and publishes the saved park GPS. Hagar Township's parks plan corroborates the kayak launch. The coordinate identifies the access area rather than a surveyed dock edge; keep it and clarify the short carry.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the published park GPS, label it as a dock/access area, and retain the under-50-yard carry and parking check.

decisions.site: Mongaup River / Upper Delaware public access near Route 97
decisions.resolvedSiteName: NPS/DEC Mongaup River Access / Route 97 carry area
decisions.coordinateRole: NPS-published public-access/parking area; not a surveyed landing point
decisions.reason: NPS identifies the Route 97 access as a public hand launch and publishes the saved coordinate. Its float guide describes a 200–300-foot uneven carry from the parking area to the water. Retain the official access-area point, label the carry, and do not call the parking GPS the landing edge.
decisions.publicationAction: Keep the NPS access-area coordinate and tell users to follow the uneven 200–300-foot carry to the hand launch.

decisions.resolvedSiteName: Longfellow Lagoon designated landing / Longfellow Gardens parking access area
decisions.coordinateRole: MCWD-published Longfellow Gardens parking/access GPS near the mandatory final landing; not a surveyed landing or dock-edge coordinate
decisions.reason: The stored latitude was about 3.1 miles north of Longfellow Gardens. MCWD's official creek map publishes 44.916125473,-93.215040979 as the Longfellow Gardens parking GPS and marks Longfellow Lagoon as the mandatory final landing before Minnehaha Falls; its canoe-landing plan corroborates the designated landing context. Correct the access-area coordinate and tell paddlers to use the marked landing and stop before the falls. Hold this route because its geometry and static maps still encode the old endpoint and cannot be regenerated/audited in this checkout.
decisions.reopeningCondition: Restore the missing @paddletoday/geo dependency, regenerate the canonical route geometry and Minnesota state/map/catalog artifacts from the corrected access GPS, inspect the route terminus and mandatory landing, run geometry and access audits, and confirm stale old-endpoint assets are absent.
